# Output Format Selection Reference

The `--output` flag — its accepted values, default, resolution precedence, and per-format dispatch.

## Overview

Output Format Selection adds one persistent global flag, `--output` (short `-o`), that selects one of four output formats per invocation. The resolved format determines which renderer a successful result is routed to: the human templates (`full` / `compact`) or the structured encoders (`json` / `yaml`).

This capability adds one flag and no command. The existing commands, their arguments, and their flags (`--include` on `me`; `--status` on `me actions` / `me projects`; `--base-url` everywhere) are unchanged. Selection makes `compact`, `json`, and `yaml` reachable from the command line for the first time.

## The `--output` flag

| Property | Value |
|---|---|
| Long name | `--output` |
| Short alias | `-o` |
| Scope | Persistent on the root command; inherited by every command |
| Values | `full` \| `compact` \| `json` \| `yaml` |
| Default | `full` |
| Matching | Case-insensitive |

- The flag is accepted anywhere on the command path. `glassfrog --output json me` and `glassfrog me --output json` resolve identically.
- Value matching is case-insensitive over exactly the four tokens: `json`, `JSON`, `Json`, and `jSON` all select `json`. Only the four token names are valid in any casing; anything else is a usage error.
- The flag appears (inert) on non-result commands (`version`, `auth …`). It has observable effect only on commands that produce result data.

## Accepted values

| Value | Renderer | stdout shape | Authoritative source |
|---|---|---|---|
| `full` (default) | human template | the labelled human projection | [Templated Human Rendering](templated-human-rendering.md) |
| `compact` | human template | one line per record, ids always present, nested collections as counts | [Templated Human Rendering](templated-human-rendering.md) |
| `json` | structured encoder | a single JSON document of the raw API payload, verbatim | [Structured Serialization](structured-serialization.md) |
| `yaml` | structured encoder | the identical data as a single YAML document | [Structured Serialization](structured-serialization.md) |

Output Format Selection selects and routes; it defines no stdout shape of its own. The same successful result feeds whichever renderer is chosen — selection changes the rendering, never which fields the command fetched.

## Affected commands

The format applies to every command that produces result data:

| Command | Synopsis |
|---|---|
| `glassfrog me` | `me [--include roles] [-o <fmt>] [--base-url …]` |
| `glassfrog me roles` | `me roles [-o <fmt>] [--base-url …]` |
| `glassfrog me actions` | `me actions [--status …] [-o <fmt>] [--base-url …]` |
| `glassfrog me projects` | `me projects [--status …] [-o <fmt>] [--base-url …]` |

## Resolution precedence

The effective format is the first source that yields a value; otherwise the built-in default:

1. `--output` / `-o` flag value
2. `GLASSFROG_OUTPUT` environment variable
3. `.glassfrogrc` `output` key (nearest-wins up the directory tree, then the home-directory file)
4. built-in default `full`

- An **absent** source is skipped to the next rung.
- A source that is **present but not one of the four tokens** is a usage error naming that source.
- Resolution always yields a format.
- The resolved source is not surfaced to the operator; the effective format is the whole need.

The format is resolved **before any API request** — the decode target depends on it — so an invalid selector fails before the network is touched. Format resolution is independent of `--base-url` resolution.

## Dispatch behavior

The resolved format selects both the decode target and the success renderer:

| Format class | Formats | Decode target | Renderer |
|---|---|---|---|
| Structured | `json`, `yaml` | raw `json.RawMessage` (verbatim 2xx capture) | the structured encoder for that format |
| Human | `full`, `compact` | the typed result struct | the human template for that format |

No format routes to a renderer other than its own.

## Error reference

| Condition | stdout | stderr | Exit code |
|---|---|---|---|
| Valid format, read + render succeed | the rendered document | — | `0` |
| `--output <bad>` (e.g. `--output xml`) | nothing (no request made) | `unsupported --output value "xml" — supported: full, compact, json, yaml` | `2` |
| `GLASSFROG_OUTPUT` or `.glassfrogrc output` holds an invalid value (flag absent) | nothing | usage error naming the source and value, e.g. `unsupported output value "xml" from GLASSFROG_OUTPUT — supported: full, compact, json, yaml` | `2` |
| `.glassfrogrc` unreadable / unparseable while resolving `output` | nothing | the config read/format error naming the file | `2` |
| Read succeeds, render fails | nothing (no partial output) | the render error message (token-free) | `1` |
| Read fails (transport / API / auth / decode) | nothing | existing cause-plus-next-step message | existing code (1/3/4/5/6) |

- Invalid-selector and resolution errors map to exit code `2` (usage error).
- Until Output-Aware Failure Rendering lands, a command failure under `json` or `yaml` keeps today's cause-plus-next-step text on stderr — it is not yet wrapped in the structured error envelope. Output Format Selection renders only its own invalid-selector usage error.
